closingKeywordRationale: #602 is an ongoing issue by design — it tracks a continuous series of example batches, and batches 1-10 have all landed against it while it stayed open. A closing keyword would end the standing series on merge, so the PR body says `Refs #602` and no close/fix/resolve keyword appears anywhere near the number.

assumptions.assumption: Batch 10 required FRESH ideation rather than a draw from batch 6's below-the-cut pool.
assumptions.rationale: Stated in issue #602 itself and re-verified against docs/ideation/realworld-function-batch6-2026-06-27.md: the pool's only two survivors are truncate-grapheme (framework-parity risk) and cron-next-fire (unbounded parsing surface), both of which the standing hard filters reject. Their risks have not changed.
assumptions.default: Ran harness:ideate for 10 new candidates; the two survivors are recorded as carried-forward hard rejects and were deliberately NOT re-scored.

assumptions.assumption: The S4 numeric pin applies to percentile-nearest-rank only; topological-task-order takes no numeric input at all.
assumptions.rationale: S4 concerns integer/fractional input contracts. order(tasks: dict[str, list[str]]) has no numeric parameter, so there is nothing to pin.
assumptions.default: percentile pins BOTH parameters explicitly (values = non-empty array of integers; p = integer in [0,100]; anything else throws, never coerces). The absence of a pin in the topological example is recorded in proposal.md as deliberate so a reviewer does not read it as an omission.

assumptions.assumption: The nearest-rank formula is written as rank = ceil((p * N) / 100) with the multiply performed BEFORE the divide.
assumptions.rationale: p * N is an exact integer, so the single division never introduces float drift and the pytest and vitest ports agree to the digit. Writing it as ceil(p/100 * N) would reintroduce exactly the drift the pin exists to remove.
assumptions.default: The ordering is stated as an explicit rule in prompt.txt, not left implicit in the formula.

assumptions.assumption: Canary's request-classification tag in each README's 'What Canary should produce' section is illustrative and verified by no test.
assumptions.rationale: Matches the same assumption recorded in the batch-9 plan.
assumptions.default: `api` for topological-task-order (structured dict input, per the lego-tracker / fifo-lot-consumer precedent) and `vitest_unit` for percentile-nearest-rank (pure scalar-returning function, per the bytes-humanizer / money-allocator precedent). Cosmetic if off.
